key_insight: FedLAB enables federated learning over multimodal graph foundation models without exposing raw client data, using traceable semantic codebooks to share useful knowledge instead of private graph contents. In simple terms, it turns rich but private graph data into transferable semantic representations that can be learned collaboratively across clients.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the challenge of training multimodal graph foundation models when graph data is distributed across clients and cannot be centrally pooled due to privacy, ownership, or regulatory constraints. The key difficulty is preserving both multimodal semantics and graph structure while still enabling effective federated collaboration.
method: Builds traceable semantic codebooks to compress multimodal graph information into shareable semantic units.
Uses a federated learning framework so clients can collaboratively train on private graph data without revealing raw text, images, attributes, or local topology.
Aligns multimodal and structural knowledge across clients to support reusable representations for graph-centric and modality-centric downstream tasks.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical path to train foundation models on sensitive graph data across organizations or devices. It can improve privacy-preserving collaboration while still leveraging diverse multimodal signals for stronger generalization and transfer.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing private multimodal graphs on multiple clients flowing into a shared semantic codebook and federated server.

paper_title: FedLAB: Traceable Semantic Codebooks for Federated Multimodal Graph Foundation Learning
paper_authors: Zekai Chen, Kairui Yang, Xuaner Chen, Xunkai Li, Xun Wu
